claim: In vitro hydrolysis of ATP in cell lysates left a substantial fraction of BiP protected from digestion by SubA, a protease that cleaves the interdomain linker.
source: It therefore came as surprise to find that in vitro hydrolysis of the ATP in cell lysates (and its conversion to ADP) left a substantial fraction of BiP protected from digestion by a specific protease (SubA) that cleaves its interdomain linker (Paton et al., 2006) (Figure 1A).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1A, which demonstrates protection of BiP from SubA cleavage after ATP hydrolysis in cell lysates.

claim: SubA is a bacterial protease that selectively cleaves the interdomain linker of BiP.
source: a specific protease (SubA) that cleaves its interdomain linker (Paton et al., 2006)
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Paton et al., 2006, which establishes SubA as a linker-specific protease.

claim: Enhancement of linker exposure by ATP was also observed in pure preparations of BiP.
source: However, similar enhancement of linker exposure was also observed in pure preparations of BiP (Figure 1B), suggesting that an intrinsic aspect of BiP's biochemistry affords the linker protection under ATP depletion and enhances its exposure upon ATP repletion.
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1B with purified BiP protein.

claim: DnaK/Hsp70-type chaperones are prone to multimerization.
source: DnaK/Hsp70-type chaperones are prone to multimerization (Freiden et al., 1992; Benaroudj et al., 1995)
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to previous studies demonstrating multimerization of these chaperones.

claim: Multimerization of DnaK/Hsp70-type chaperones is enhanced in their ADP-bound state.
source: which is enhanced in their ADP-bound state (King et al., 1995; Schonfeld et al., 1995)
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to studies showing enhanced multimerization in the ADP-bound state.

claim: Crystal forms of bacterial DnaK show the interdomain linker of one protomer engaged as a typical substrate by an adjacent protomer.
source: Crystal forms of a bacterial DnaK have been observed in which the interdomain linker of one protomer is engaged as a typical substrate by an adjacent protomer (Chang et al., 2008).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to a crystallographic study by Chang et al., 2008.

claim: The V461F mutation in BiP interferes with substrate engagement at the SBD.
source: BiPV461F, a mutation that interferes with substrate engagement at the SBD (Laufen et al., 1999; Petrova et al., 2008)
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to studies characterizing the V461F mutation.

claim: The ADDA mutation (L414VLL417 to A414DDA417) abolishes the linker's role in allostery.
source: a four residue substitution that alters the hydrophobic nature of the interdomain linker (L414VLL417 to A414DDA417, referred to as BiPADDA henceforth) abolishing the linker's role in allostery (Laufen et al., 1999)
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Laufen et al., 1999, which characterized the ADDA mutation.

claim: The ADDA mutation disrupts the SubA cleavage site in BiP.
source: disrupting the SubA cleavage site (Paton et al., 2006)
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Paton et al., 2006.

claim: The ADDA mutation alters key residues that render the linker a BiP/Hsp70 substrate.
source: altering key residues that render the linker a BiP/Hsp70 substrate (Chang et al., 2008)
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Chang et al., 2008.

claim: The ADDA mutation preserves the intrinsic ability of BiP's SBD to bind other substrates.
source: all whilst preserving the intrinsic ability of BiP's SBD to bind other substrates
evidence: The claim is based on inference from the characterization of the ADDA mutation.

claim: Size-exclusion chromatography of purified wildtype BiP yields three discernable peaks (I, II, and III) with tailing into the high molecular weight region.
source: Size-exclusion chromatography (SEC) of purified wildtype BiP yields three discernable peaks (arbitrarily named I, II and III) with tailing into the high molecular weight region (Figure 2A, black trace), consistent with previous observations (Chevalier et al., 1998).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2A and a citation to previous work.

claim: The molar masses of BiP complexes in elution peaks I, II, and III match closely the predicted masses of BiP monomers, dimers, and trimers, respectively.
source: The molar masses of BiP complexes in elution peaks I, II and III, as measured by multi-angle light scattering (SEC-MALS), match closely the predicted masses of BiP monomers, dimers and trimers, respectively (Figure 2—figure supplement 1).
evidence: The claim is supported by SEC-MALS data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1.

claim: Addition of ATP leads to redistribution of BiP from higher molecular weight fractions into a single large peak.
source: Addition of ATP leads to redistribution of BiP from the higher molecular weight fractions into a single large peak that elutes slightly later than peak I (Figure 2B).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2B.

claim: The late elution of the ATP-induced peak is consistent with linker-mediated compaction of the SBD and NBD.
source: The late elution of the ATP-induced peak is consistent with linker-mediated compaction of the SBD and NBD (Swain et al., 2007).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Swain et al., 2007, and inference from the SEC data.

claim: BiPV461F elutes mostly in peak I on size-exclusion chromatography.
source: BiPV461F elutes mostly in peak I and its elution is also slightly retarded by ATP (Figure 2A, purple trace and Figure 2C)
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2A and 2C.

claim: BiPV461F has intact allostery and structural integrity.
source: pointing to intact allostery and structural integrity of the mutant
evidence: The claim is inferred from the ATP-dependent elution behavior of BiPV461F.

claim: BiPADDA is preferentially distributed into the late-eluting peak I on size-exclusion chromatography.
source: BiPADDA elutes with less sharply-defined peaks. Like BiPV461F it too is preferentially distributed into the late-eluting peak I (Figure 2A, green trace)
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2A.

claim: Addition of ATP has no effect on the migration of BiPADDA on size-exclusion chromatography.
source: Importantly, addition of ATP had no effect on the migration of BiPADDA (Figure 2D), consistent with abolition of allosteric coupling between the domains by the alteration of the hydrophobic linker (Laufen et al., 1999; Swain et al., 2007; Kumar et al., 2011).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2D and citations to previous studies.

claim: Competition by a BiP substrate peptide (HTFPAVL) dissociates higher molecular weight forms of BiP and increases intensity of peak I.
source: Competition for BiP's SBD either by a well-characterized BiP substrate peptide, (HTFPAVL [Marcinowski et al., 2011]), or a peptide corresponding in sequence to the interdomain linker (DTGDLVLLD), dissociated the higher molecular weight forms of BiP and increased intensity of peak I, whereas a peptide derived from the BiPADDA mutant linker sequence (DTGDADDAD) had no effect (Figure 2E).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2E and a citation to Marcinowski et al., 2011.

claim: A peptide corresponding to the interdomain linker (DTGDLVLLD) dissociates higher molecular weight forms of BiP.
source: Competition for BiP's SBD either by a well-characterized BiP substrate peptide, (HTFPAVL [Marcinowski et al., 2011]), or a peptide corresponding in sequence to the interdomain linker (DTGDLVLLD), dissociated the higher molecular weight forms of BiP and increased intensity of peak I
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2E.

claim: A peptide derived from the BiPADDA mutant linker sequence (DTGDADDAD) has no effect on BiP oligomerization.
source: whereas a peptide derived from the BiPADDA mutant linker sequence (DTGDADDAD) had no effect (Figure 2E)
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2E.

claim: Incorporation of fluorescent peptide as a function of BiP quantity falls progressively with increased complex size.
source: Incorporation of peptide as a function of BiP quantity fell progressively with increased complex size. The ratio of fluorescent to quantity signal (RFLU/A230 nm), arbitrarily set to 1.00 for peak I, was 0.48 for peak II and 0.26 for peak III (Figure 2F)
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2F.

claim: Peaks I, II, and III are constituted of progressively larger BiP oligomers with no concordant increase in peptide binding capacity.
source: suggesting that peaks I, II and III were constituted of progressively larger BiP oligomers but with no concordant increase in peptide binding capacity
evidence: The claim is inferred from the fluorescent peptide binding data in Figure 2F.

claim: BiP oligomers are arranged such that the SBDs of all but the ultimate protomer are engaged in linker binding.
source: The latter finding is consistent with oligomers arranged such that the SBDs of all but the ultimate protomer are engaged in linker binding (Figure 1C).
evidence: The claim is inferred from the peptide binding data and the proposed model in Figure 1C.

claim: In the presence of BiPADDA, LY-BiPV461F tracer distributes between a lower molecular weight peak I and higher molecular weight peak II.
source: In the presence of BiPADDA, the LY-BiPV461F tracer distributed between a lower molecular weight peak I and higher molecular weight peak II consistent with a complex formed between BiPADDA and the LY-BiPV461F tracer (Figure 3B).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3B.

claim: The higher molecular weight peak II is much diminished when BiPADDA is replaced by the compound mutant BiPADDA;V461F.
source: The latter was much diminished when BiPADDA was replaced by the compound mutant BiPADDA;V461F, which is unable to engage substrate (Figure 3C).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3C.

claim: Exposure of samples to SubA prior to SEC eliminates the fluorescent signal at peak I, replacing it with a later-eluting peak (CP).
source: Exposure of the samples to SubA prior to SEC eliminated the fluorescent signal at peak I, replacing it with a later-eluting peak (tentatively labeled 'CP', for cleavage product) (Figure 3B,C, right panels).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3B and 3C.

claim: The BiPADDA-dependent fluorescent peak II is notably resistant to SubA.
source: However, the BiPADDA-dependent fluorescent peak II was notably resistant to SubA (Figure 3B)
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3B.

claim: BiP deleted of its helical lid (BiPlidless) still forms linker-dependent oligomers that dissociate upon exposure to ATP.
source: However, BiP, deleted of its helical lid (BiPlidless), still formed linker-dependent oligomers that dissociated upon exposure to ATP (Figure 3—figure supplement 1A,B)
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1A,B.

claim: BiPlidless engages peptides in a hierarchy similar to that of wildtype BiP oligomers.
source: engaged peptides in a hierarchy similar to that of wildtype BiP oligomers (compare Figure 2F with Figure 3—figure supplement 1C)
evidence: The claim is supported by comparison of experimental data in Figure 2F and Figure 3—figure supplement 1C.

claim: BiPlidless protects the interdomain linker of LY-BiPV461F tracer similarly to wildtype BiP.
source: and protected the interdomain linker of LY-BiPV461F tracer similarly to wildtype BiP (Figure 3—figure supplement 1D)
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1D.

claim: The helical lid is dispensable for BiP oligomerization via linker engagement.
source: These observations point to the dispensability of the helical lid for BiP oligomerization via linker engagement
evidence: The claim is inferred from the experimental data with BiPlidless.

claim: The linker is engaged by the SBD as a typical substrate in a configuration consistent with the crystal structure of G. kaustophilus DnaK.
source: and support the conclusion that the linker is engaged by the SBD as a typical substrate in a configuration consistent with the crystal structure of G. kaustophilus DnaK (Chang et al., 2008)
evidence: The claim is supported by inference from the experimental data and a citation to Chang et al., 2008.

claim: ATP binding has two opposing effects on interdomain linker exposure: protection against SubA by burial at the interface of the coupled NBD and SBD, and exposure to SubA by release of the linker from the SBD of adjacent protomers in the oligomer.
source: The aforementioned observations pointing to a mechanism of oligomerization that entails linker engagement suggest that ATP binding has two opposing effects on interdomain linker exposure: (i) Protection against SubA by burial at the interface of the coupled NBD and SBD; a state that equilibrates relatively rapidly with the uncoupled linker-exposed state, leading ultimately to complete digestion by SubA. (ii) Exposure to SubA by release of the linker from the SBD of adjacent protomers in the oligomer.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the experimental observations with SubA cleavage.

claim: In the absence of ATP, BiP oligomers are very stable with a low off rate.
source: In the absence of ATP the oligomers are very stable with a low off rate (Figure 2—figure supplement 3B).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 3B.

claim: ATP enhances cleavage of wildtype BiP by SubA whilst attenuating cleavage of the V461F mutant.
source: In case of the wildtype BiP, effect ii was seen to dominate, but in BiPV461F (that is unable to engage the linker in its SBD), effect i dominates (Figure 4A).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4A.

claim: Wildtype BiP forms discrete oligomers (labeled II, III, IV, and V) on native gel electrophoresis.
source: Wildtype BiP formed discrete oligomers (labeled II, III, IV and V), whilst BiPV461F populated a dominant high mobility species (I) (Figure 4B).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4B.

claim: BiPV461F populates a dominant high mobility species (I) on native gel electrophoresis.
source: whilst BiPV461F populated a dominant high mobility species (I) (Figure 4B)
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4B.

claim: Exposure to SubA does not completely disassemble oligomeric BiP species but converts them to a new series of higher mobility.
source: Exposure to SubA did not completely disassemble the oligomeric species, but rather converted them to a new series of higher mobility (compare lanes 1 and 2 in Figure 4B).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4B.

claim: In the presence of ATP, wildtype BiP is digested to near completion by SubA, with the NBD as the dominant remaining species.
source: However, in the presence of ATP, wildtype BiP was digested to near completion by SubA, with the NBD as the dominant remaining species (the SBD is not resolved on the native gel) (lane 4, Figure 4B)
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4B.

claim: Peptide competition biases oligomeric BiP species towards higher mobility forms that are converted to a new series of even higher mobility by SubA.
source: Peptide competition had a similar, though less pronounced effect as ATP, biasing the oligomeric species towards higher mobility forms that were converted to a new series of even higher mobility by SubA (Figure 4C).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4C.

claim: The concentration of BiP at which half of species II (K1/2maxII) dissociates is 0.45 µM.
source: The concentration of BiP at which half of species II (K1/2maxII) and half of species III (K1/2maxIII) dissociated was 0.45 µM and 0.74 µM, respectively (Figure 4—figure supplement 1).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1.

claim: The concentration of BiP at which half of species III (K1/2maxIII) dissociates is 0.74 µM.
source: The concentration of BiP at which half of species II (K1/2maxII) and half of species III (K1/2maxIII) dissociated was 0.45 µM and 0.74 µM, respectively (Figure 4—figure supplement 1).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1.

claim: The discrete oligomeric species observed in native gel electrophoresis of wildtype BiP are diminished in BiPADDA.
source: The discrete oligomeric species observed in native gel electrophoresis of wildtype BiP were diminished in BiPADDA (Figure 5A, compare lanes 1 and 3)
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5A.

claim: BiPT37G and BiPG226D mutations promote oligomerization.
source: Both the BiPT37G and BiPG226D mutations that cannot attain the ATP-induced coupled conformation ([Wei et al., 1995] and Figure 5—figure supplement 1 and Figure 5—figure supplement 2) promoted oligomerization, in sharp contrast to BiPADDA (Figure 5A).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5A and supplementary figures, and a citation to Wei et al., 1995.

claim: BiPT37G and BiPG226D cannot attain the ATP-induced coupled conformation.
source: Both the BiPT37G and BiPG226D mutations that cannot attain the ATP-induced coupled conformation ([Wei et al., 1995] and Figure 5—figure supplement 1 and Figure 5—figure supplement 2)
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Wei et al., 1995, and experimental data in supplementary figures.

claim: Oligomers formed by BiPT37G and BiPG226D mutants are unaffected by ATP.
source: As predicted, the oligomers formed by the BiPT37G and BiPG226D mutants were unaffected by ATP, in contrast to wildtype BiP (Figure 5A)
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5A.

claim: The resistance of oligomers formed by BiPT37G and BiPG226D mutants to dissociation by ATP correlates with protection of the interdomain linker from cleavage by SubA.
source: The resistance of oligomers formed by the BiPT37G and BiPG226D mutants to dissociation by ATP, correlated with protection of the interdomain linker from cleavage by SubA (full-length BiP in Figure 5B)
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5B.

claim: Defective oligomerization of BiPADDA is imposed in cis by altered composition of the mutant interdomain linker.
source: Together, these observations separate the allosteric effects of the ADDA mutation from its effects on oligomerization and support that defective oligomerization of BiPADDA is imposed in cis, by altered composition of the mutant interdomain linker.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the comparison of BiPADDA with BiPT37G and BiPG226D mutants.

claim: Incorporation of pBpa at positions located in the vicinity of the interdomain linker (L414, L416, L417, L419) results in UV-dependent crosslinks with FLAG-tagged wildtype BiP.
source: When combined with purified FLAG-tagged wildtype BiP, derivatives decorated with pBpa at positions located in the vicinity of the interdomain linker (L414, L416, L417, L419) resulted in a conspicuous, UV-dependent shift in the mobility of the unmodified FLAG-tagged BiP on denaturing SDS-PAGE (Figure 6B).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 6B.

claim: Incorporation of pBpa at residues distant from the interdomain linker (R510 and T518) gives rise to a much weaker crosslink signal.
source: By contrast, incorporation of pBpa at residues distant from the interdomain linker (R510 and T518) gave rise to a much weaker crosslink signal (Figure 6B, lanes 12 and 14 and Figure 6—figure supplement 1C).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 6B and Figure 6—figure supplement 1C.

claim: Native gel electrophoresis confirms the presence of discrete higher molecular weight species of BiP in cell lysates.
source: Native gel electrophoresis confirmed the presence of discrete higher molecular weight species of BiP in cell lysates, which stand out above the heterogeneous signal expected of a chaperone that engages many substrates [as previously noted, (Freiden et al., 1992)].
evidence: The claim is supported by native gel electrophoresis data and a citation to Freiden et al., 1992.

claim: BiP oligomers in cell lysates are further stabilized by ATP depletion.
source: These were further stabilized by ATP depletion (Figure 7A).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 7A.

claim: The migration of oligomeric BiP species from cell lysates on native gels is similar to that of untagged mature BiP (19–654) purified from bacteria.
source: The migration of these oligomeric species on native gels was similar to that of untagged mature BiP (19–654), purified from bacteria (Figure 7B).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 7B.

claim: Cleavage by SubA leads to the appearance of a similar set of cleavage products in cell lysates and purified BiP.
source: Moreover, cleavage by SubA led to the appearance of a similar set of cleavage products, suggesting that the in vivo oligomers may also be comprised of one BiP protomer engaging the interdomain linker of another at its SBD.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the comparison of cleavage products in cell lysates and purified BiP.

claim: FLAG-tagged BiPS649A and FLAG-tagged BiPADDA;S649A are incorporated into discrete high molecular weight species in cells.
source: Both FLAG-tagged BiPS649A and FLAG-tagged BiPADDA;S649A were incorporated into discrete high molecular weight species (Figure 7C).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 7C.

claim: Exposure of lysate from cells transfected with FLAG-tagged BiPS649A to SubA yields cleavage products.
source: Exposure of the lysate from the cells transfected with FLAG-tagged BiPS649A to SubA yielded the familiar pattern of cleavage products in the anti-FLAG immunoblot (Figure 7C, lanes 3 and 4).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 7C.

claim: FLAG-tagged BiPADDA;S649A-containing oligomers are completely resistant to cleavage by SubA.
source: The FLAG-tagged BiPADDA;S649A was also incorporated into indistinguishable higher molecular weight species, however, unlike the endogenous BiP in the same lysate, the FLAG-tagged BiPADDA;S649A-containing oligomers were completely resistant to cleavage by SubA (Figure 7C, lanes 5 and 6).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 7C.

claim: Oligomers of FLAG-tagged BiPV461F formed in the presence of untagged BiPADDA are strongly protected from SubA-mediated cleavage.
source: By contrast, oligomers assembled in the presence of the (untagged) BiPADDA were strongly protected from SubA-mediated cleavage (Figure 7D, lane 9).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 7D.

claim: Oligomers of FLAG-tagged BiPV461F formed in the presence of untagged BiPADDA are maintained when ATP is added to the lysate.
source: In addition, the oligomers of FLAG-tagged BiPV461F formed in the presence of untagged BiPADDA were maintained when ATP was added to the lysate (Figure 7D, lane 10).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 7D.

claim: Exposure of cells to cycloheximide diminishes both defined BiP oligomers and generalized intra-lane background, replacing them with a prominent high mobility species (labeled 'B' form).
source: Exposure of cells to the protein synthesis inhibitor cycloheximide had a profound effect on the distribution of anti-BiP reactive species in the native gel. Both the defined oligomers and the generalized intra-lane background (the latter likely reflecting BiP interactions with unfolded client proteins) were diminished and replaced by a prominent high mobility species (labeled 'B' form, Figure 8A, lanes 1 and 2).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 8A.

claim: The accumulation of the 'B' form of BiP is blocked by addition of novobiocin, an inhibitor of ADP ribosylation.
source: The accumulation of the 'B' form was blocked by addition of novobiocin, an inhibitor of ADP ribosylation, which also restored the oligomers in the cycloheximide-treated sample (Figure 8A, lane 7).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 8A.

claim: Activation of Fv2E-PERK by AP20187 leads to accumulation of the 'B' form of BiP, apparently at the expense of oligomeric forms.
source: Activation of a modified eIF2α kinase, Fv2E-PERK, by a dimerising drug AP20187 [that sidesteps the normal induction of ER stress but inhibits translation initiation (Lu et al., 2004)], also led to accumulation of the 'B' form of BiP, apparently at the expense of oligomeric forms of BiP (Figure 8B, lane 5).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 8B and a citation to Lu et al., 2004.

claim: Dissociation of BiP oligomers and appearance of the 'B' form occur on a timescale previously reported for accumulation of ADP ribosylated BiP or AMPylated BiP in cycloheximide-treated cells.
source: Kinetic analysis showed concordance between dissociation of the oligomers and appearance of the 'B' form (Figure 8—figure supplement 1A), which furthermore occurred on a timescale previously reported for accumulation of ADP ribosylated BiP (Laitusis et al., 1999) or AMPylated BiP (Ham et al., 2014) in cycloheximide-treated cells.
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data in Figure 8—figure supplement 1A and citations to Laitusis et al., 1999, and Ham et al., 2014.

claim: Challenging cells with agents that perturb the protein folding environment in the ER leads to diminution of oligomers without a commensurate increase in the 'B' form.
source: Challenging cells with agents that perturb the protein folding environment in the ER and thereby increase BiP's clientele also led to diminution of oligomers, but without a commensurate increase in the 'B' form. This was evident in cells treated with the glycosylation inhibitor tunicamycin, the proline analog azetidine and the reducing agent dithiothreitol (DTT) and is consistent with competition between substrates and other BiP molecules for the chaperone's SBD (Figure 8C,D and Figure 8—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 8C, 8D, and Figure 8—figure supplement 1B.

claim: Thapsigargin, an ER lumenal calcium-depleting agent, promotes BiP oligomerization.
source: The ER lumenal calcium-depleting agent, thapsigargin, a strong activator of the UPR (Wong et al., 1993), stood out as an important exception: Unlike the other manipulations, which activate the UPR by affecting the structure of ER client proteins, thapsigargin, an inhibitor of the smooth ER calcium reuptake (SERCA) pump that depletes ER calcium (Sagara and Inesi, 1991), promoted BiP oligomerization (Figure 8C, lane 5).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 8C and citations to Wong et al., 1993, and Sagara and Inesi, 1991.

claim: The effect of thapsigargin on BiP oligomerization is dominant to that of cycloheximide.
source: This effect of thapsigargin was dominant to that of cycloheximide (which favors the 'B' form over oligomers, Figure 8C, lane 4)
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 8C.

claim: The effect of thapsigargin on BiP oligomerization is dominant to that of tunicamycin, azetidine, or DTT.
source: and to that of agents that directly perturb ER client protein structure: Tunicamycin (Figure 8D, lane 4), azetidine (Figure 8D, lane 6) or DTT (Figure 8D, lane 11).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 8D.

claim: The distribution of BiP into oligomeric forms follows rapidly upon depletion of lumenal calcium, being observed within 10 min of application of thapsigargin.
source: The distribution of BiP into oligomeric forms followed rapidly upon depletion of lumenal calcium, being observed within 10 min of application of thapsigargin (Figure 9A, compare lanes 2 and 3), a point at which lumenal calcium levels [assessed by the fluorescent ER calcium probe, D1ER cameleon (Palmer et al., 2004)] declined markedly (Figure 9B).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 9A and 9B, and a citation to Palmer et al., 2004.

claim: BiP oligomerization is sustained throughout the period of lumenal calcium depletion.
source: Oligomerization was sustained throughout the period of lumenal calcium depletion and was noted well before the thapsigargin-mediated attenuation in the levels of the 'B' form of BiP (Figure 9A, lane 6).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 9A.

claim: The mobilization of the modified 'B' form of BiP by ER calcium depletion occurs on a timescale that is too long to account for the rapid increase in BiP oligomers upon ER calcium depletion.
source: The latter observation suggests that the well documented mobilization of the modified (presumably ADP-ribosylated/AMPylated) 'B' form of BiP by ER calcium depletion (Laitusis et al., 1999; Ham et al., 2014) occurs on a timescale that is too long to account for the rapid increase in BiP oligomers upon ER calcium depletion
evidence: The claim is inferred from the kinetic data and citations to Laitusis et al., 1999, and Ham et al., 2014.

claim: A pool of BiP, distinct from the 'B' form, is tapped for oligomerization early upon calcium release.
source: and that a pool of BiP, distinct from the 'B' form, is tapped for oligomerization early upon calcium release
evidence: The claim is inferred from the kinetic observations.

claim: Similar observations regarding BiP oligomerization were made in CHO-K1 cells exposed to the calcium ionophore A23187.
source: Similar observations were made in CHO-K1 cells exposed to the calcium ionophore A23187, pointing to the role of lumenal calcium fluctuations (as opposed to some other effect of thapsigargin) in the re-distribution of BiP amongst its various forms (Figure 9C,D).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 9C and 9D.

claim: Application of ATP to the growth medium of CHO-K1 cells leads to a rapid and transient depletion of lumenal calcium stores.
source: As expected, application of ATP to the growth medium led to a rapid and transient depletion of lumenal calcium stores (Hayashi and Su, 2007) (Figure 10A).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 10A and a citation to Hayashi and Su, 2007.

claim: Application of extracellular ATP to CHO-K1 cells is correlated with a rapid and transient increase in BiP oligomers.
source: This was correlated with a rapid and transient increase in BiP oligomers, observed over a similar time frame (Figure 10B).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 10B.

claim: Extracellular ATP-induced BiP oligomerization is attenuated by the phospholipase C blocking drug U73122.
source: Extracellular ATP was linked to BiP oligomerization through a canonical signaling cascade, as it was attenuated by simultaneous application of the phospholipase C blocking drug U73122 (Figure 10C, lane 4).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 10C.

claim: Phospholipase C inhibition has no effect on thapsigargin's ability to promote BiP oligomerization.
source: Phospholipase C inhibition had no effect on the downstream-acting thapsigargin's ability to promote BiP oligomerization (Figure 10C, lane 6)
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 10C.

claim: ER calcium depletion leads to diminished recovery of BiP in complex with a misfolded truncated ER client protein, the null Hong Kong allele of α1-antitrypsin.
source: ER calcium depletion led to diminished recovery of BiP in complex with a misfolded truncated ER client protein, the product of the null Hong Kong allele of α1-antitrypsin (Liu et al., 1997), introduced by transfection into CHO-K1 cells (Figure 11A).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 11A and a citation to Liu et al., 1997.

claim: The complex between BiP and immunoglobulin heavy chain partially dissociates in thapsigargin-treated cells.
source: Similar observations were made in regard to the complex between BiP and immunoglobulin heavy chain (IgHC, expressed in the absence of the light chain); it too was observed to partially dissociate in thapsigargin-treated cells (Figure 11B).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 11B.

claim: Cholecystokinin promotes dissociation of amylase from BiP in AR42j cells.
source: Cholecystokinin also promoted dissociation of amylase, a major secretory product of pancreatic acinar cells, from BiP (Figure 11C).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 11C.

claim: BiP associated with amylase is diminished by cholecystokinin in AR42j cells.
source: Reciprocally, BiP associated with amylase was also diminished by cholecystokinin (Figure 11D).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 11D.

claim: The BiP:amylase complex that is diminished by calcium depletion in vivo is sensitive to ATP in vitro.
source: The BiP:amylase complex that was diminished by calcium depletion in vivo was also sensitive to ATP in vitro (Figure 11D, lane 4), confirming that it represented engagement of a conventional client by BiP.
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 11D.

claim: ER lumenal calcium depletion, induced by a physiological ligand that promotes BiP oligomerization, disfavors interaction of endogenous BiP with an endogenous client.
source: These findings confirmed that ER lumenal calcium depletion, induced by a physiological ligand that promotes BiP oligomerization, also disfavored interaction of endogenous BiP with an endogenous client.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the experimental observations with amylase and BiP.

claim: There is a negative correlation between BiP oligomerization and client binding.
source: Together, these observations establish a negative correlation between BiP oligomerization and client binding.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the experimental observations.

claim: BiP oligomers form by engagement of the hydrophobic interdomain linker of one BiP protomer as a typical substrate of an adjacent BiP protomer.
source: BiP oligomers were observed here to form by engagement of the hydrophobic interdomain linker of one BiP protomer as a typical substrate of an adjacent BiP protomer.
evidence: The claim summarizes the main finding of the study.

claim: BiP oligomerization is rapidly tuned to the physiological state of the cell.
source: BiP oligomerization is rapidly tuned to the physiological state of the cell
evidence: The claim is supported by the experimental observations showing rapid changes in oligomerization.

claim: The oligomeric form of BiP is a relatively inactive storage form of the chaperone that is accessible on a short time scale.
source: and given that oligomerization inactivates participating BiP protomers, the oligomeric form is a relatively inactive storage form of the chaperone that is accessible on a short time scale
evidence: The claim is inferred from the experimental observations and the proposed model.

claim: Competition between oligomerization and substrate binding buffers the ER against rapid fluctuations in unfolded protein load in both directions.
source: Our findings are consistent with a model whereby competition between oligomerization and substrate binding buffers the ER against rapid fluctuations in unfolded protein load in both directions.
evidence: The claim is the main conclusion of the study, inferred from the experimental observations.

claim: The interdomain linker of Hsp70 chaperones consists of a short stretch of aliphatic residues, well suited to engage the SBD.
source: The interdomain linker of Hsp70 chaperones consists of a short stretch of aliphatic residues, well suited to engage the SBD (Flynn et al., 1989; Blond-Elguindi et al., 1993).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: A crystal form of bacterial DnaK shows the engagement of two highly conserved aliphatic side chains of the linker in hydrophobic sites of the SBD.
source: A crystal form of bacterial DnaK with cross-protomer binding of the interdomain linker in the SBD shows the engagement of two highly conserved aliphatic side chains of the linker in hydrophobic sites of the SBD (Chang et al., 2008).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to a crystallographic study.

claim: The mode of BiP oligomerization results in removal of the BiP protomers involved from the pool of active chaperones.
source: Given the role of these very same side chains in allosteric coupling between the NBD and SBD, this mode of BiP oligomerization results in removal of the BiP protomers involved from the pool of active chaperones.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the structural and functional data.

claim: The proposed architecture of BiP oligomers fits with the observation of a single peptide binding site available in BiP oligomers formed in vitro, regardless of their size.
source: The proposed architecture of the oligomers (Figure 1C) fits well with our finding of a single peptide binding site available in BiP oligomers formed in vitro, regardless of their size (Figure 2F).
evidence: The claim is inferred from the experimental data and the proposed model.

claim: Oligomeric forms of Hsp70 are holdases rather than foldases.
source: The model fits the observation that oligomeric forms of Hsp70 are holdases rather than foldases (Blond-Elguindi et al., 1993; Thompson et al., 2012)
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: DnaK oligomers formed in vitro are subject to regulation by the nucleotide exchange factor, GrpE.
source: The model also explains the observation that DnaK oligomers formed in vitro are subject to regulation by the nucleotide exchange factor, GrpE (Thompson et al., 2012)
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to a previous study.

claim: The concentration of BiP in the ER is greater than 200 µM.
source: Nonetheless, the high concentration of BiP in the ER (>200 µM, [Ghaemmaghami et al., 2003])
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Ghaemmaghami et al., 2003.

claim: The inherent affinity of BiP protomers for one another is consistent with a model whereby oligomerization and substrate binding compete with each other on a level playing field.
source: and the inherent affinity of BiP protomers for one another, are consistent with a model whereby oligomerization and substrate binding compete with each other on a level playing field.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the affinity measurements and the proposed model.

claim: Enhanced production of unfolded proteins rapidly draws on the pool of inactive, oligomeric BiP to service its growing clientele.
source: Our observations paint a coherent picture whereby enhanced production of unfolded proteins rapidly draws on the pool of inactive, oligomeric BiP to service its growing clientele.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the experimental observations.

claim: The ER is unusual in possessing alternative mechanisms for inactivating its Hsp70 protein, BiP, by covalent modification (ADP ribosylation) and AMPylation.
source: The ER is unusual in possessing alternative mechanisms for inactivating its Hsp70 protein, BiP, by covalent modification (ADP ribosylation) (Freiden et al., 1992; Laitusis et al., 1999; Chambers et al., 2012) and AMPylation (Ham et al., 2014).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: The modified form of BiP appears to equilibrate with the active pool more slowly than the oligomers.
source: The modified form of BiP appears to equilibrate with the active pool more slowly than the oligomers.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the kinetic observations.

claim: The physiological impact of both oligomerization and modification is to enable the cell to avoid the cost of over-chaperoning without having to degrade surplus BiP as stress is resolved.
source: Either way it seems likely that the physiological impact of both oligomerization and modification is to enable the cell to avoid the cost of over-chaperoning (Dorner et al., 1992; Feder et al., 1992) without having to degrade surplus BiP as stress is resolved
evidence: The claim is speculative, based on inference from the experimental observations and citations to previous studies.

claim: Oligomerization and modification provide cells with an inactive reserve of BiP to draw upon as stress mounts, without resorting to activation of the translational and transcriptional arms of the UPR.
source: and to provide cells with an inactive reserve of BiP to draw upon as stress mounts, without resorting to activation of the translational and transcriptional arms of the UPR.
evidence: The claim is speculative, based on inference from the experimental observations.

claim: The inverse correlation between unfolded protein burden and BiP oligomerization appears to break down in the context of ER calcium depletion.
source: The inverse correlation between unfolded protein burden and BiP oligomerization appears to break down in the context of ER calcium depletion, which is both a strong inducer of the UPR and promotes rapid oligomerization of BiP.
evidence: The claim is based on the experimental observations.

claim: BiP oligomerization upon calcium depletion correlates with less substrate binding.
source: This apparent paradox needs to be considered in the context of observations that BiP oligomerization upon calcium depletion also correlates with less substrate binding (a feature first noted many years ago [Suzuki et al., 1991] and confirmed here)
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data and a citation to Suzuki et al., 1991.

claim: Oligomerization appears to be the primary event triggered by ER calcium efflux from BiP's perspective.
source: From BiP's perspective, oligomerization appears to be the primary event triggered by ER calcium efflux.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the kinetic observations.

claim: Oligomerization depletes the pool of active chaperones and disrupts, by mass action, chaperone-client interactions, releasing clients that would otherwise have remained bound to BiP.
source: This depletes the pool of active chaperones and disrupts, by mass action, chaperone-client interactions, releasing clients that would otherwise have remained bound to BiP.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the experimental observations.

claim: The ensuing, slower loss of the modified form of BiP is consistent with equilibrium between the modified form and the monomer.
source: The ensuing, slower loss of the modified form of BiP is consistent with equilibrium between the modified form and the monomer
evidence: The claim is inferred from the kinetic observations.

claim: In vitro, there is no measureable effect of calcium on BiP oligomerization, in either the ATP state or ADP state or in the presence of the J-factor ERdj3 or the exchange factor GRP170.
source: In vitro, there is no measureable effect of calcium on BiP oligomerization, in either the ATP state or ADP state or in the presence of the J-factor ERdj3 or the exchange factor GRP170 (not shown)
evidence: The claim is based on experimental observations (not shown).

claim: In vivo, ER calcium depletion promotes BiP oligomerization.
source: yet in vivo, ER calcium depletion promotes such oligomerization
evidence: The claim is based on experimental observations.

claim: An ER-localized J-factor whose affinity for BiP as a substrate is increased selectively as (Ca+2)ER declines could account for BiP favoring itself as a client (oligomerizing) over other clients.
source: This discrepancy could be resolved by an ER-localized J-factor whose affinity for BiP as a substrate is increased selectively as (Ca+2)ER declines. Given that the affinity of Hsp70 proteins for their substrates is governed by J-protein driven non-equilibrium mechanisms (De Los Rios and Barducci, 2014), such a scenario could account for BiP favoring itself as a client (oligomerizing) over other clients, as (Ca+2)ER declines.
evidence: The claim is speculative, based on inference and a citation to De Los Rios and Barducci, 2014.

claim: One consequence of (Ca+2)ER depletion-mediated BiP oligomerization would be to shift the equilibrium between unfolded proteins and active chaperones in favor of the former.
source: Regardless of mechanism, one consequence of (Ca+2)ER depletion-mediated BiP oligomerization would be to also shift the equilibrium between unfolded proteins and active chaperones in favor of the former.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the experimental observations.

claim: The monomer of BiP likely serves as a UPR repressor.
source: Furthermore, given the 1:1 stoichiometry of the repressive complex formed between BiP and the lumenal, stress-sensing domains of the UPR transducers PERK and IRE1 (Bertolotti et al., 2000), it seems likely that the monomer serves as a UPR repressor.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the stoichiometry of the BiP-UPR transducer complex and a citation to Bertolotti et al., 2000.

claim: (Ca+2)ER depletion-mediated oligomerization of BiP stands to contribute to UPR activation by increasing the burden of free unfolded proteins and by lowering the availability of monomeric BiP to repress the stress transducers.
source: Thus, (Ca+2)ER depletion-mediated oligomerization of BiP stands to contribute to UPR activation by increasing the burden of free unfolded proteins and by lowering the availability of monomeric BiP to repress the stress transducers.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the experimental observations and the proposed model.

claim: Calcium depletion-mediated oligomerization of BiP is observed in physiological circumstances, as a consequence of engagement of cell surface receptors by activating ligands that couple to store release channels.
source: Calcium depletion-mediated oligomerization of BiP is observed in physiological circumstances, as a consequence of engagement of cell surface receptors by activating ligands that couple to store release channels.
evidence: The claim is based on experimental observations with extracellular ATP and cholecystokinin.

claim: The transient excursions of UPR signaling imposed by BiP oligomerization may couple signals that promote granule secretion to transient translational repression in secretory cells.
source: However, it is tempting to speculate that the transient excursions of UPR signaling imposed by BiP oligomerization may have some benefit. In secretory cells, such a scheme would couple signals that promote granule secretion to transient translational repression (attendant upon PERK activation [Harding et al., 1999]).
evidence: The claim is speculative, based on inference and a citation to Harding et al., 1999.

claim: Transient translational repression may have short-term benefits in terms of diverting resources away from translation to the bio-energetically costly process of secretion.
source: This may have short-term benefits in terms of diverting resources away from translation to the bio-energetically costly process of secretion.
evidence: The claim is speculative.

claim: Transient activation of UPR transducers results in elaboration of downstream effectors (XBP1, ATF6, and ATF4) that adapt cells to their secretory mission by promoting ER biogenesis and expanding the capacity to translate mRNAs.
source: Transient activation of UPR transducers also results in elaboration of downstream effectors. These transcription factors, XBP1, ATF6 and ATF4, adapt cells to their secretory mission by promoting the latent process of ER biogenesis (Sriburi et al., 2004; Lee et al., 2005), and by expanding the capacity to translate mRNAs (Harding et al., 2003).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: Calcium depletion-mediated BiP oligomerization may contribute to transient activation of the UPR observed in secretory cells responding to secretagogues.
source: It is thus tempting to speculate that calcium depletion-mediated BiP oligomerization contributes to transient activation of the UPR observed in secretory cells responding to secretagogues (Kubisch and Logsdon, 2007)
evidence: The claim is speculative, based on inference and a citation to Kubisch and Logsdon, 2007.

claim: Calcium depletion-mediated BiP oligomerization may promote long-term coupling of the capacity to produce and process precursors of secretory proteins to the short-term demand for the secreted end product.
source: and thereby promotes long-term coupling of the capacity to produce and process precursors of secretory proteins to the short-term demand for the secreted end product.
evidence: The claim is speculative.
